newsitem.title: UK: British firm launches breathable fast-chill gas.
newsitem.headline: British firm launches breathable fast-chill gas.

text.p: A British company Thursday launched a breathable, liquefied version of air that could create temporary cold storage space in minutes and provide super-cold conditions for testing aircraft engines.
BOC Group Plc said the product, a mixture of liquid oxygen and liquid nitrogen, represented a major breakthrough because it is the first gas of its kind that could be breathed safely.

Food retailers have shown great interest in the gas, which would allow companies to turn anything from giant warehouses to small rooms into temporary chilled stores without using massive refrigeration equipment, it said.
"If you need a cold store for one day a week or two hours a day then there is some technology to do it," said Deb Chatterji, BOC's managing director of technology

"The only limit on this is the limit of our imaginations," he said, adding that annual sales could eventually "be north of 20 million pounds ($32 million) and south of 200 million pounds" ($324 million).

BOC originally wanted to find a way of enabling refrigerated trucks to keep their loads cool over "multi-drop" deliveries, which meant finding a gas that someone entering the back of the truck could breathe.
People cannot breathe liquid nitrogen, the current mainstay of refrigeration.

A number of companies, including Air Products and Chemicals Inc., of Lehigh Valley, Pa., are believed to have studied the complex storage problems created by liquefied air, which has a temperature of minus 191 degrees centigrade. But BOC is the first to launch the gas commercially.

It has already been tested on poultry farms, where it dramatically cut death rates caused by high summer temperatures, BOC said. It could eventually be used to air condition rock concert venues or to create extreme-temperature test chambers for the aerospace and other high-tech industries.
BOC said it would make a decision about expanding production and overseas marketing at the end of the year.
